PART I
Purpose, scope and definitions
§1. Purpose
This synthetic notice demonstrates an amendment to a fictional overseas recruitment fee
framework. It is written to support controlled testing of document understanding, evidence
verification, operational impact investigation, and human approval workflows.
§2. Scope
The notice applies only to the fictional licensed recruitment agencies, synthetic employment
contracts, synthetic policies, and synthetic deployment files included in the RegOps
demonstration corpus.
§3(a). Migrant worker
A synthetic person represented in the demonstration corpus as seeking or holding an
overseas employment placement. No real person is represented by this definition.
§3(b). Placement fee
Any recruitment service charge, agency commission, placement charge, documentation
handling charge, or equivalent amount collected directly or indirectly from a migrant worker
as a condition of recruitment or deployment.
§3(c). Employer-paid administrative cost
A documented cost paid by the employer and not recovered from the worker through wages,
deductions, deposits, reimbursements, or a related-party payment.
§3(d). Shadow amendment
A proposed contract change applied only to an isolated synthetic copy for preview and
revalidation. A shadow amendment does not alter an authoritative source contract.

PART II
Operative fee amendments
§4(a). Worker-paid placement fees
No licensed recruitment agency shall charge a migrant
worker any placement fee; permissible costs are limited to
those defined in §4(b).
For this synthetic amendment, the maximum placement fee payable by a migrant worker is
BDT 0. A fee may not be collected through a wage deduction, deposit, reimbursement,
related-party payment, or another arrangement with the same effect.
§4(b). Permissible employer-paid costs
An employer may pay documented administrative costs and required medical examination
costs. The agency must not recover those amounts from the worker directly or indirectly. A
worker-facing contract must describe the worker's payable amount as BDT 0.
§5(a). Fee schedule publication
Each licensed recruitment agency must reissue its published fee schedule within 30 days
after this amendment is issued. The reissued schedule must identify the BDT 0 worker-paid
placement fee limit and distinguish employer-paid costs.
§5(b). Internal policy review
An annual-review policy is not sufficient by itself. Any internal policy or appendix that retains
the prior fee schedule must be marked for update before the effective date.
§6. Medical examination exception
Employer-paid medical examination costs remain permissible under this amended synthetic
rule when no amount is transferred to, deducted from, or reclaimed from the worker.
§7. Effective date
The provisions in Part II take effect on 1 October 2026.

SYNTHETIC MOBILITY STANDARDS AUTHORITY
NOT A REAL REGULATION

PART III
Transition, records and review
§8(a). Existing synthetic contracts
Before the effective date, an agency must review each active synthetic contract that
requires a worker-paid placement fee, recruitment service charge, documentation charge, or
equivalent payment.
§8(b). Existing synthetic deployment files
A deployment file recording a fee collected before the effective date must be queued for
fee-reconciliation review. This notice does not state that the earlier synthetic payment was
unlawful and does not authorize an automated refund.
§9. Controlled amendments
A proposed amendment to an active synthetic contract must remain a draft until an
authorized human reviewer approves or rejects it. Rejection must not execute the draft,
resolve the underlying finding, or change the source contract.
§10. Evidence retention
The demonstration system should retain the source document identifier, page number,
exact quoted text, related synthetic record identifier, action outcome, and authoritative run
transition needed to explain each finding.
§11. Duplicate prevention
A repeated attempt to create or execute the same controlled action for the same run and
finding must not create a second action or a second approval decision.
§12. Non-authoritative model output
Automated extraction and impact investigation results are candidates only. They become
authoritative demonstration records only after deterministic schema, citation, identity,
binding, and policy verification succeeds.
END OF SYNTHETIC
 NOTICE
This fictional document exists solely for the RegOps
demonstration. All agencies, workers, contracts, policies, cases,
obligations, findings, and decisions connected to it are synthetic.
